concepts.name: contentTokens.join('') === content at every observation point
quota failure on one conversation never blocks persisting the others

reviewer_findings.description: Single STORAGE_KEY write is all-or-none, so the invariant holds by construction. But post-S1-fix a double quota failure is swallowed per AC-ERR-4: nothing persists and the caller cannot tell. No AC covers signaling failed persistence. src/lib/chat.ts:172 is the signal point for any story that adds a notice. Tracked as S1-F9.

concepts.name: N concurrent first-calls on one (baseUrl, model) issue exactly one /api/show

reviewer_findings.description: AC-PERF-1 holds and is stronger than at S3 implementation. loadVocab stores the catch-wrapped promise synchronously before any await, so concurrent first calls share one POST /api/show; a failed load is evicted before the rejection reaches awaiters and can be retried. The 3-entry LRU evicts only SETTLED entries (settlement tracked in a WeakSet fed by promise.finally on the same object the map holds), and failure cleanup deletes by promise identity, closing the stale-rejection-evicts-a-live-entry hole an earlier LRU draft had opened. Pinned by an integration test loading 4 keys with the 3rd in flight, asserting both directions. UNDISTURBED by the token_type threading (that happens inside fetchVocab, inside the cached promise; keying and identity untouched). Residual S3-T2: the cap is a steady-state target, not a hard ceiling - one eviction per touch, touch-driven.

concepts.name: tokenize / tokenize.result / tokenize.error correlate by requestId, not conversationId

reviewer_findings.description: Closed on all three axes. Correlation: requestId-keyed, sited ahead of the conversationId-drop guard in handleServerMessage. Lifecycle: immediate reject on a dropped send (send() now returns boolean), 10s timeout, try/catch around send, cancelPendingTokenize on socket close; every exit path clears the timer and deletes the map entry before settling, so no double-settle and no entry outlives its promise. Shape: asTokenizeResponse validates every field of both variants and returns null on anything malformed, so a holed message falls through to timeout rather than resolving with undefined tokens. Covers the widened too_large union unchanged, since it validates typeof reason === 'string' rather than enum membership.

concepts.name: boundary source is exactly one of stream | computed | pending | unavailable
token separator is U+2502, never ASCII pipe
Ollama-only capabilities gate on ProviderConfig.type, never provider name

reviewer_findings.description: SINGLE-OWNER RESTORED and survives the too_large widening. An S3 draft had widened resolveProvider from private to public so ws-handler could read config.type itself, splitting the gate across two modules with two failure shapes. Now: LlmRouter.tokenizeText mirrors showModelMeta, resolveProvider is private again, ws-handler imports only the error class and does protocol mapping. Error->reason mapping is total (UnsupportedProviderError, VocabUnavailableError, else internal). Provider id threads from the conversation through the wire to resolveProvider, closing the modelProviderMap last-writer-wins hole where one model name served by two providers could tokenize against the wrong one. The too_large cap is correctly sited in ws-handler BEFORE the router call - a transport/DoS concern, not a provider-capability one - so it does not re-fragment the gate.

tests/fixtures/*.json.gz, inflated via node zlib in test setup

reviewer_findings.description: Convention and reality agree. An S3 draft shipped gzip bytes under a plain .json extension while architecture.md Constraint 8 and this concept both declare *.json.gz; the lead adjudicated for the declared convention and the fixture was renamed, with all 8 stale references corrected including the normative glossary at acceptance-criteria.md and spec.md (verified path-only: no AC wording, ID or numbering altered). Survives the token_type extension: still .json.gz, still gzip, ids 0-294 byte-identical with 295-296 appended, goldens independently re-derived and unchanged. The capture script stays congruent - its tokenizer.ggml.* prefix filter picks up token_type with no script change.

reviewer_findings.description: Expected token count MUST derive from the recorded eval_count + done_reason, never by counting the fixture's own content chunks - deriving from chunk count restores the tautology while keeping the fixture, and nothing structural prevents that. Known limits: n=2, qwen3:1.7b, Ollama 0.30.8, frozen, capture denominator unrecorded.

concepts.name: ConversationStep declared twice (server/types.ts, src/types/chat.ts), kept congruent by hand with no structural enforcement

reviewer_findings.description: ConversationStep declared twice and kept congruent by hand; no structural or test enforcement. tsc -p tsconfig.json is already red for unrelated reasons so even incidental compilation signal is unreadable. S2 adds boundary-source shape, S3 tokenize payloads, S4 reconciliation figures - drift surface compounds each story.

Improved but still load-bearing. Down from three copies to two: backend-client.ts now imports TokenizeRequestMessage/TokenizeResponseMessage and types its outgoing literal, so the client's wire usage is compile-checked against a declaration for the first time in this epic. The server/src pair stays hand-maintained by design (Boundary Rule 1). NOTE WHY too_large moved cleanly across both declarations: the client validates shape, never enum membership, so a ONE-SIDED widening would have passed typecheck and tests just as cleanly - this change did not actually exercise the congruence risk. The first field consumed BY VALUE on both sides is where it bites; S4's reconciliation figures are the likely candidate. CARRY TO S4.

concepts.name: onDelta hands out the same mutable step objects processStreamLine keeps mutating; contentTokens grows under a stable step id
a computed boundary set is valid only for the model it was computed under; the cache key must include the model

reviewer_findings.description: ENFORCED. An S3 draft keyed the computed cache on (step.id, step.content) with model-free effect deps, while the real source closed over the conversation's model - so a model switch left old-model boundaries under AC-UX-8's 'computed under the conversation's current model' notice. Now keyed on (step.id, step.content, cacheKeySuffix) with chat-workspace passing selectedConversation?.model. Critically the S2-F2/S2-F8 ref-read-through invariant survives: computedSource is still absent from the effect deps and hasComputedSource is still the stable boolean, so invalidation happens via the key rather than via identity. Pinned by a test varying ONLY the suffix.

concepts.name: a socket-close handler may only cancel work correlated to that socket's own bookkeeping; cancelling a chat stream must be distinguishable from a user-initiated stop

reviewer_findings.description: HOLDS. An S3 remediation wired the whole of cancelAll() into onClose, which also rejected in-flight chat streams with Error('AbortError') - the exact sentinel chat-workspace uses to mean 'the user pressed stop' - so a transient reconnect rendered as 'Generation stopped.'. Narrowed to cancelPendingTokenize(), which drains only the tokenize map. Pinned by a test that invokes the captured onClose and asserts cancelPendingTokenize fired once and cancelAll never did. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LEAD: cancelAll() is now caller-less, and the pre-epic 'chat stream hangs forever when the socket drops mid-stream' behavior it would have covered is back at baseline. Outside every S3 AC - routed to BACKLOG as S3-T1, deliberately not a further remediation round.

concepts.name: load-bearing claims about systems outside this repo, which this repo's tests structurally cannot falsify
concepts.rationale: S3's severity-7 (the cl100k vs Qwen digit rule) lived in a line the incremental reviewer read three times and recorded as 'internally consistent by construction', having correctly named it the top target for a cold cross-vendor pass. The warning was right; it was not a finding, and the pass never ran because the configured backend was unavailable. The ledger had no state for 'asserted, not verified' - every concept resolves to true/false - so the claim decayed into prose in a snapshot string instead of sitting in a re-verification queue. This concept IS that queue.

reviewer_findings.description: DIVISION OF LABOUR, for S4 and every later story. All 27 findings the incremental reviewer produced across three rounds were seam, lifecycle or contract defects - the class a ledger-backed accumulated model is genuinely strong at. It produced ZERO external-claim findings, and could not: a comment asserting upstream behavior plus a fixture built from that same assertion are self-consistent, so more passes by the same reader cannot separate them. Cold cross-vendor review is not a redundancy check over the incremental pass; it is the ONLY detector for this class. Treat it as a gate: when unavailable, record the story as CONDITIONALLY closed with its external claims listed, rather than closed.

reviewer_state.cross_story_model_snapshot: S1+S2+S3 closed. S3 took 4 remediation rounds: severity 7 -> 5 -> 3 -> (cold pass) 7 -> closed. WHAT THE LEDGER LEARNED, and why external-claims-register now exists as a concept type: the incremental reviewer produced 27 findings across three rounds, ALL seam/lifecycle/contract defects, ZERO external-claim defects. It cannot produce the latter - a comment asserting upstream behavior plus a fixture built from that same assertion are self-consistent, so re-reading separates nothing. It DID correctly name the exact line and the exact reason, which is the most that role can do; the gap was that a named-but-unverifiable claim had no ledger state between 'resolved' and 'open', so it decayed into prose. Four such claims are now registered as EC-1..EC-4 with explicit status, and S4 inherits them as a queue rather than a warning. TREAT THE CROSS-VENDOR PASS AS A GATE - it was unavailable once here and a severity-7 rode through three clean-looking rounds as a result; a gate that fails open is not a gate. VERIFIED GOOD ACROSS ALL ROUNDS, do not re-litigate: S2-F4's streaming-TextDecoder fix; S2-F11's harness fold-in; the AC-PERF-1 in-flight promise cache with settled-only eviction and identity-guarded failure cleanup; the single-owner provider-type gate (survives the too_large widening, correctly sited in ws-handler); the tokenize wire contract end to end (correlation, lifecycle, shape); and the load-bearing tests - AC-TOK-7's six-string golden loop, AC-TOK-2's per-index decodeTokenIds check, AC-TOK-6's property (fc.string({unit:'binary'}), 300 runs), AC-DEP-1's merge-rank-swap test (the ONLY pin on min-vs-max tie-break) and the new fixture-independent digit test (independently confirmed to fail against the old regex) - all unweakened, with goldens independently re-derived in round 4. CARRY TO S4: (1) re-measure the AC-STRUCT-3 budget before planning; roughly 32 of 60 chat-workspace.tsx lines remain. (2) convention-duplicated-step-type survived too_large only because the client validates shape, never enum membership - S4's reconciliation figures are the first fields likely consumed BY VALUE on both sides, which is where it actually bites. (3) COMPUTED_MISMATCH_REASON already anticipates AC-TOK-5's wrong-source risk; do NOT add a second mismatch check downstream of resolveBoundarySource - whichever layer drops boundaries owns the label. (4) the vocab LRU is a steady-state target, not a hard cap; S4 adds another tokenize consumer and another (baseUrl, model) pair. (5) EC-2 bounds what any S4 claim about token counts can honestly assert: AC-TOK-7 proves algorithm class, not model fidelity, until a host re-captures the fixture. (6) S1-F9/S2-F5 persistence-signal gap still unowned; routes at wrap-up.
